title: Discobox desktop bridge
description: What crosses the pipe between `discobox desktop` and its app: the JSON messages, the payloads of the terminal frames, and the frame kinds. Generated from the Go types in cli/internal/console/bridge by its genwire command; no field is ever null.

input.description: Bytes typed into a stream's terminal (app).

resize.description: A stream's terminal size, a ResizePayload (app).

exit.description: A stream's end; its payload is why, empty when it ended cleanly (CLI).

repaint.description: Asks for a stream's screen again (app); no payload.

Message.description: Message is one JSON message: its type, and the body of that type.

oneOf.description: TypeHello opens the bridge (app).
TypeWelcome answers it with the protocol, the spec and the session (CLI).
TypeSubscribe and TypeUnsubscribe start and stop a topic (app).
TypeSnapshot is a topic's value, whole, on subscribe and on every change (CLI).
TypeCommand runs a registry command (app).
TypeResult ends a command or an upload (CLI).
TypeForm is a form a command needs filled (CLI); TypeSubmit fills it (app); TypeFieldErrors is the core's refusal of what was submitted (CLI).
TypeQuestion is a question a running command asks (CLI); TypeAnswer answers it (app).
TypeProgress is a running command's report, warning or acceptance (CLI).
TypeEdit is a file for the app to open in the user's editor (CLI); TypeSaved is the app's word that it was saved (app).
TypeUpload is a pasted or dropped image for a box (app).
TypeOpen attaches a stream the app allocated to a session, and TypeClose detaches it, ending nothing in the box (app).
TypeStream is a stream's state: attached, failed, reconnecting, reconnected (CLI). Its output and its end are frames on the stream.
TypeFollow is a link pressed in a pane, for the core to say where it goes (app); a result answers it.
TypeDraft is the prompt in the app's composer, to be kept for the next window (app).

Hello.description: Hello is the app's first message.

Welcome.description: Welcome answers hello. Spec and Session are sent only when the protocols match: another version's fields may not parse.

Spec.description: Spec is the console's spec as a frontend is handed it.

colors.description: Colors is every color token by name, in both palettes.

dimensions.description: Dimensions is every space, radius and stroke token by name, in points.

states.description: States and Agents are the glyphs, by state.

gestures.description: Gestures are the bindings that are not commands (Gesture): every key a frontend's list, tree, leader and panes bind is a command's or one of these.

menus.description: Menus are the desktop's menus, in the order its menu bar draws them.

linkSchemes.description: LinkSchemes are the schemes of the links in a pane the console answers itself (BoxLinkSchemes): a press on one, plain or with the link modifier, is the console's and never the program's or the OS's.

SpecColor.description: SpecColor is one color token: its dark and light values as #rrggbb, and the xterm-256 index the TUI draws it with (0 where it uses none).

Glyph.description: Glyph is how a state is drawn: its shape, the color token it is drawn in, and the word that stands for it where there is no color. An empty Color is the surrounding text's.

SpecCommand.description: SpecCommand is one registry command as a frontend is handed it. Every list is present, empty where there is nothing in it.

SpecTarget.description: SpecTarget is what a command takes, as a frontend is handed it.

oneOf.description: SpecTargetBox is a command that takes a box.
SpecTargetWindow is one that takes none: it acts on the window.

SpecBindings.description: SpecBindings is a command's bindings, keyed by frontend (598 §2).

SpecTUIBinding.description: SpecTUIBinding is TUIBinding on the wire.

SpecDesktopBinding.description: SpecDesktopBinding is DesktopBinding on the wire. Menu is omitted for a gesture.

Menu.description: Menu is one of the desktop's menus.

oneOf.description: MenuSession is a workspace's sessions: a pane's own menu too.

SpecGesture.description: SpecGesture is one gesture as a frontend is handed it.

Session.description: Session is what the window is opened on.

primaryServer.description: PrimaryServer is the configured server's name.

directory.description: Directory and Branch are where the CLI was run, which a create cuts from.

draft.description: Draft is the prompt the last window on this machine left in its composer, which this one opens holding.

Subscribe.description:
Subscribe starts following a topic. Sub is the app's, unique for the bridge's life; Box is the box key, for a topic about one box. Filter is what the listing is narrowed to, which a renderer holds as the TUI holds its List's (console/DESIGN.md, "The list"): the app subscribes again under a new Sub to change it, and ends the old. Without one the listing opens on the filter this machine's last window left (console.ListView). Reveal, a box's key, narrows it instead to what shows that box whatever the filter hid (console.Revealing): a view the palette navigates to, which is never saved over the person's filter.

The commands and the palette are about where the app asks from (Context) and, for the commands, the boxes it names (Targets). They are read from the last listing, never the servers, and sent again as it changes; the app subscribes again under a new Sub when what it asks changes — each query of the palette, a menu opened somewhere else.

Topic.description: Topic is what a subscription follows.

oneOf.description: TopicListing is the boxes, across every server.
TopicResources is what Discobox has on this machine and is using.
TopicRequests is the credential and approval requests waiting on a person, and the credentials refused.

TopicProvisioning is what a box that is not usable yet is being made to do (Box). It says what an attach waits on, and runs until it is unsubscribed — once the box is provisioned it says "connecting to the terminal" — so the app ends it when the box's primary attaches.
TopicAudit is a box's audit timeline, followed (Box).

TopicHeader is what a box's workspace header says of it, as the core says it (console.Header), with its ports forwarded to this machine for as long as the subscription lasts: the workspace's forward, which goes with the screen showing it (Box).
TopicSessions is what a box's workspace opens: its sessions and its services' tabs, as the core orders and names them (Box).
TopicCommands is every registry command as it stands where the app asks from, for the boxes it names (Context, Targets): what its menus list, enabled or with why not.
TopicPalette is what the palette finds for a query (Context, Palette): the core's results, in the core's order.
TopicComposer is what a create from the composer would be made with, as the line under it says it (console.RunOptions.Summary): sent again whenever the run options change.

Filter.description: Filter is what the listing is narrowed to (console.Filter): a server, a folder (by its key; none is every folder), the tags a box must carry, and whether the archived are listed.

Context.description: Context is where the command is asked from (console.Context): navigation is the app's, and the core is handed the parts of it its rules read.

workspace.description: Workspace is the key of the box whose workspace the window holds.

PaletteQuery.description: PaletteQuery is what the palette asks (console.PaletteQuery): the text typed, at most one chip — a command by its ID, or a box by its key — and whether archived boxes are in scope. Current is the key of the box the window is on, and Recent the boxes it has gone to, latest first: navigation is the app's, and what an empty query ranks by.

Snapshot.description: Snapshot is a topic's value, whole. Error is why it could not be read this time; the last value stands until one can. Exactly one value is set for the topic, unless Error is.

Listing.description: Listing is the box listing as the console shows it (console.List): every box listed, and the rows the filter shows, in the order they are drawn.

boxes.description: Boxes is every box listed, on every server and whatever the filter: what a box is looked up in, and what the palette searches.

rows.description: Rows are the boxes the filter shows, as drawn: folder sections when Grouped, and in each a box followed by the boxes it created.

grouped.description: Grouped is whether the rows are drawn in sections, one per folder.

notes.description: Notes are what the list says about servers after its rows.

filter.description: Filter is what the rows are narrowed to.

label.description: Label is how the filter reads: "all discoboxes", or what it narrows the rows to. Narrowed is whether it leaves any box out by what it is (console.List.Narrowed): an empty list then says nothing matches, not that there is nothing.

choices.description: Choices are every way to narrow the rows, counted against the filter as it stands (console.List.FilterChoices).

archived.description: Archived is how many more rows showing the archived would draw.

unreachable.description: Unreachable are servers that did not answer; Waiting, ones still being asked with nothing of theirs to show.

Box.description: Box is one box as the app draws its row.

key.description: Key is what the app names the box by in every message: its ID when one server is configured, the server's name and the ID otherwise. Opaque to the app, which shows ID.

dirty.description: Dirty is uncommitted work; Ahead, clean commits beyond the spawn commit (console.Sandbox.Uncommitted, Ahead).

cpu.description: CPU and MemoryBytes are what a box that is up is using; none for one that is not.

attachable.description: Attachable is whether the box has a container to open now.

State.description:
State is a sandbox's user-facing lifecycle state, narrowed to the six the launcher draws. The server reports more of them — stopping, archiving, deleting — but a picker only has to answer "can I act on this", and the transitional states answer that the same way the state they are heading for does.

Repairing is kept apart from starting, which it is drawn like: a repair recorded and not yet landed, typed or automatic (ADR 26-10-12-711 §8). The box had failed, and the row says it is being rebuilt rather than that it is coming up for the first time.

oneOf.description: StateSuspended is a box frozen whole, its memory kept (ADR 26-10-16-420): up as far as acting on it goes — stop takes it — and off as far as anything inside it answering, which a start or a use brings back.

Row.description: Row is one box's place in the list (console.List.Rows, Nesting): its section, how deep it is nested under the box that created it, and what it says in place of its name when picked out.

section.description: Section is the key of the folder section it is drawn in, and SectionTitle how that section is headed.

depth.description: Depth is how many creators it is nested under; Last, whether it is its creator's last row; Rules, for each level between the top and its creator, whether a branch carries on past it there.

remark.description: Remark is what the row says in place of its name when picked out.

origin.description: Origin is the machine it was created on, when that is not this one.

Remark.description: Remark is console.Remark: the text, and the command that answers it when one does, with what doing so does as a verb. The app spells the command's key with its own binding.

Note.description: Note is a line the list draws about a server rather than a box.

FilterChoice.description: FilterChoice is one way to narrow the listing (console.FilterChoice): the filter marking it makes, and for a marked tag the one letting it go.

ChoiceGroup.description: ChoiceGroup is which of the filter's three parts a choice is in.

Resources.description: Resources is the machine's capacity and use. Known is false until there is something measured to show.

Requests.description: Requests is what waits on a person.

Request.description: Request is one item waiting on a person. Box is the key of the box that asked, as the listing names it.

RequestKind.description: RequestKind is what a request waits on a person for.

oneOf.description: RequestCredential is a credential the box asked for.
RequestRefresh is a credential to sign in again for.
RequestTrust is a host whose certificate the box asked to trust.
RequestAdoption is a box asking to be adopted.
RequestAPIAccess is a box asking for access to the Discobox API.

Rejection.description: Rejection is a credential refused where a person is needed. Boxes are the listed boxes it affects (console.RejectionsFor): a harness's credential is refused for every box running that harness.

Provisioning.description: Provisioning is what a box is being made to do now; empty once nothing is reported.

Audit.description: Audit is a box's audit timeline: its most recent records, oldest first, and the trails the last read could not reach.

AuditRecord.description: AuditRecord is one line of the timeline.

Header.description: Header is what a box's workspace header says (console.Header): each field the core's answer, their order and colors the app's.

work.description: Work is the issue and the pull request the box's tags number, each a link to it.

blocked.description: Blocked is what a box waiting on a person says in place of the git word, empty for one that is not.

base.description: Base is the work's git position; Changes its state as a word (dirty, ready, clean), empty when there is nothing to say. Tone is how both read, and Ready a ready pull request over ready work, which reads as done.

diff.description: Diff is whether the box has reported a change, and Added and Deleted the lines it changed.

desktop.description: Desktop is the box's graphical desktop, once its forward has bound it.

ports.description: Ports is what the box serves, by protocol, web first; a forwarded web port links to its local end.

tags.description: Tags is the box's tags the header says nothing of otherwise, labeled.

unforwarded.description: Unforwarded is why the box's ports could not be forwarded, when they could not: they are listed, unlinked.

agent.description: Agent is what the box's agent is doing (a program status state: working, idle, blocked, done, error), and AgentMsg what it says of it (console.Header.Agent): the core's choice between what the program in the box's attached primary reports over OSC 7501 and the listing's poll. None when there is nothing to say.

Link.description: Link is something in the header a press opens in the browser; one without a URL is text.

GitTone.description: GitTone is how a header reads the work's git position and word.

oneOf.description: ToneQuiet is clean work, or work nothing is known about.
ToneDirty is uncommitted work.
ToneAhead is committed work beyond what the box was cut from.

PortGroup.description: PortGroup is one protocol's ports, in port order.

Sessions.description:
Sessions is what a box's workspace opens, by the core's rules, in tab order (console.Exec.Before): the tabs of its services worth one (console.ListedServiceTabs), the primary, and every session the exec listing opens as a tab. Running is false for a box that is not running: only its primary opens, and attaching it is what waits for the box.

A session's tab is never closed by a snapshot: its stream says when it ends. A service's tab is, since the service listing is the whole truth about a declaration (console.Workspace.ReconcileServices): a service tab the app holds that is not listed, or is listed on another Run, has nothing left to draw, and goes.

Tab.description: Tab is one session as the app draws its tab. Kind is the column and what it is.

service.description: Service is the declared service a service's tab draws; its Exec is the service's (console.ServiceTabID), not any one run's. Run is the run it draws (console.Service.RunKey): one that moves — a restart, a stop, a fix — is a tab to open again. Status is what it says over its screen while its service is not running: its state, its card under it.

tool.description: Tool is the tool a tool's tab runs, by its ID: what the tools menu finds a running tool's tab by.

TabKind.description: TabKind is what a session is, which says the column its tab is in.

oneOf.description: TabPrimary is the box's primary session, its harness.
TabTerminal is another harness terminal.
TabShell is a shell.
TabTool is a tool's session.
TabService is a declared service's session.

Commands.description: Commands is every registry command as it stands, in the registry's order.

Entry.description: Entry is one command as it stands: whether it can act, and why not. Uses is how often this window has used it, which ranks the palette.

Palette.description: Palette is what a query found, in the order the palette lists it. Archived is whether archived boxes were searched: asked for, or brought in by a chip that acts only on them, which the app keeps. Commit is the chip the query's text committed as it was typed (console.PaletteCommit): the rows are the committed query's, and the app takes its chip and text in place of its own. Partial and Stale are what the search says about the servers it searched (console.List.Partial, Stale): those it has no rows from yet or could not reach, and those whose rows are behind — every server, whatever the list's filter.

PaletteRow.description: PaletteRow is one result: a box by its key, or a command as it stands; Why is why it cannot be chosen, when it cannot.

PaletteCommit.description: PaletteCommit is a command committed as the palette's chip, and the text left after it.

Composer.description: Composer is the summary of what a create would be made with: the harness, and every other run option somebody chose (console.RunOptions.Summary).

Chip.description: Chip is one part of it: its words, and whether it was chosen rather than a default, which the app draws lit.

Command.description: Command runs a registry command. ID is the app's, unique for the bridge's life, and is what its result, forms, questions and progress name. Targets are box keys, explicit: a box command never falls back to what is on screen.

Args.description:
Args are what a command takes beyond its targets: the stream a session it makes is attached to and the size of its pane (shell, terminal), the session it acts on (end, repaint), for services one of the box's services and the verb to run on it — without them, services lists them for its menu — and for new the prompt in the composer, which the box is given to do.

The harnesses command reads the harnesses of Server (the list's server; empty for the primary) for its page, or, with a Harness and an Action, does that to it: Path is the file a files action edits. The review config command reads a box's harness changes for its review, or, with a Change and the Candidate the review showed, saves or discards that candidate.

tool.description: Tool names one of the box's tools for the tools command: with no File it is run — handed the box, for one that runs on this machine, or its session made on Stream — and with File, that file of it is edited.

ServiceVerb.description: ServiceVerb is a lifecycle action against one of a discobox's declared services. Like a HarnessVerb it runs against the API and returns, leaving the window up: a service is not something you sit in front of, so acting on one never takes the screen.

HarnessAction.description: HarnessAction is one thing the harnesses page does to a harness.

oneOf.description: HarnessActionVariant creates a variant following the harness's bundle with an account of its own (HarnessVariantForm).
HarnessActionDefault makes it the project's default.
HarnessActionConfig shows its config card (HarnessCard).
HarnessActionFiles edits one of its files in the person's editor (DataSource.EditHarnessFile).
HarnessActionReset resets it to its bundle's defaults, asking first (Harness.ResetQuestion).

HarnessChange.description: HarnessChange is what a review of a box's harness changes does with the candidate it shows.

oneOf.description: HarnessChangeSave saves the candidate as the harness's shared settings and logins.
HarnessChangeDiscard drops it, leaving the box's own files as they are.

Result.description: Result ends a command (or an upload or a follow, by its ID).

box.description: Box is the box the flow entered is about.

session.description: Session is the session a shell or terminal made, attached to the command's stream.

entries.description: Entries are what the palette and the action menu list, as they stand for the command's context and targets.

services.description: Services are the box's declared services, in declaration order, read as the services menu opens: what it lists.

path.description: Path is where an upload landed in the box.

url.description: URL is where a followed link goes, for the app to open.

harnesses.description: Harnesses are the harnesses of the server the harnesses command read, in the order they were registered: what its page lists, read again after each action, which leaves the one it acted on as Harness. A variant created is Harness.

card.description: Card is a harness's config card (console.HarnessCard), for its config action.

changes.description: Changes is a box's harness changes, read as its review opens.

tools.description: Tools are a box's tools as the tools menu lists them (console.PickerTools), read as it opens, and Addresses its two addresses to copy beside them (console.AddressOffers).

Status.description: Status is how a command ended.

oneOf.description: StatusDone is a command the core carried out; Note says what came of it.
StatusFailed is one refused or that failed; Why says why.
StatusCanceled is one whose form or question was dismissed.

StatusEnter is one whose flow is the app's: the core has ruled it can run, and the app enters it — moving focus, opening a page or a menu, opening the box's workspace (Box). For new it is the box made, or, with no Box, a prompt that is the window's way out (console.LeavesWindow): the app leaves, as quit does.

Service.description: Service is one declared service, as the services menu lists it: its name, what it is doing and what it is for or why it cannot run (Detail), and its verbs as they stand for it (console.Service.Actions).

ServiceAction.description: ServiceAction is one verb a service's menu offers, and why it cannot act when it cannot.

Harness.description: Harness is one of a server's harnesses as the harnesses page lists it: what its row says, its files for the files action's picker, and its actions as the core offers them (console.Harness.Actions).

age.description: Age is how long ago it last changed, as the list says an age.

HarnessFile.description: HarnessFile is one of a harness's files: its path, its size in bytes, and what the core says of it (console.HarnessFile.Notes).

HarnessOffer.description: HarnessOffer is one action as a harness's menu offers it, and why it cannot act when it cannot.

CardRow.description: CardRow is a row of a card (console.CardRow): its label, empty where it carries on the row above's; its value in spans; and a file's first lines under it, with More how many more it has.

CardSpan.description: CardSpan is a stretch of a card row's value, in its tone.

CardTone.description: CardTone is how a renderer draws a stretch of a card's value.

oneOf.description: CardPlain is the value itself.
CardQuiet is said about the value, beside it.
CardStandout is the one word on the card that stands out: the default.
CardCommand is a command line.

HarnessChanges.description: HarnessChanges is a box's harness changes as its review shows them (console.HarnessChanges): the candidate, where it stands, what it changes, what saving does, and what the review offers to do with it. Nothing is what the review says of a candidate carrying nothing to save, empty for one that carries something.

ChangedFile.description: ChangedFile is one file a candidate adds, updates or removes, as its diff, headed as the core heads it (console.HarnessChangedFile.Label).

ChangeOffer.description: ChangeOffer is what the review offers to do with the candidate, and why it cannot when it cannot.

Tool.description: Tool is one of a box's tools as the tools menu lists it: what it is called and what it is (running, when the box has its session live), whether it runs on this machine, why it cannot run when it cannot (console.Tool.Why), and the files it carries to edit.

ToolFile.description: ToolFile is one file a tool carries, by its name, and what its row says of it (console.ToolFileDetail): where it lands in a box, and where its copy is on this machine.

Address.description: Address is one of a box's addresses to copy (console.AddressOffer): its label, and the address, or why there is none.

Form.description:
Form is a form a command needs filled, described by the core. ID is the CLI's; it is sent again, same ID, with Applies recomputed, after a draft is submitted.

Fields can grow as they are answered — a repeated run option gains a field once its last is filled — so a form sent again after a draft may hold more fields than before, matched to what the app holds by Key. Note is what the answers so far add up to (the command a create would run), said under the fields; Action is what the button that submits it says, empty for the app's own word.

Field.description: Field is one field of a form (console.Field). Value is what it holds as the core reads it: as it opens (console.Field.Opens — a typed value as one line, a picker's chosen key), or after a draft what the answers so far make it. Applies is whether it takes an answer given the answers so far; one that does not is drawn with Why in place of its value.

Choice.description: Choice is one option of a picker field, or an answer to a question.

Submit.description: Submit fills a form. Answers are the fields the person changed, by key; every other field answers what it opened holding, so an untouched field is never an edit. Cancel dismisses it. Draft asks only for the form again with Applies recomputed for these answers, and submits nothing.

FieldErrors.description: FieldErrors is why submitted answers were refused; the form stays up holding them. An error with no Field is about the answers as a whole.

Question.description:
Question is what a running command asks (console.Question). With Choices it is a pick of one; with none, a yes or no answered "yes" or "no".

Subject is what it is about, on a line of its own above the body.

Answer.description: Answer answers a question, exactly once: Key, or Declined when it cannot be asked. A yes or no dismissed is answered "no", never declined (console's Question): only a pick of one is declined when it is dismissed.

Progress.description: Progress is what a running command says: a step, a warning, or the box a create made the moment the server took it.

Edit.description: Edit is a file on this machine for the app to open in the user's editor.

Saved.description: Saved is the app's word that the person is finished with an edit, exactly once: Canceled when they gave it up, which saves nothing, and Error when it could not be opened.

Upload.description: Upload is an image pasted or dropped on a box. It is answered with a result, by ID, whose Path is where the image is in the box.

Open.description: Open attaches the stream the app allocated to one of a box's sessions, sized for its pane. Frames the app sends on it before it is attached are kept until it is, and dropped if it fails.

Close.description: Close detaches a stream: the app no longer shows it. The session goes on in the box; ending one is the end command.

Stream.description: Stream says a stream's state changed. A failed stream is forgotten. End is what an ending, or a failure to attach, does to the workspace; Status is what a held tab says over its last screen.

StreamState.description: StreamState is where a stream stands.

oneOf.description: StreamEnded is the session's program ending, and End what that does to the workspace (console.Tab.End). The stream's Exit frame follows.

TabEnd.description: TabEnd is what a session's ending does to its workspace (console.TabEnd).

oneOf.description: EndWorkspace: the primary ended, and the workspace with it.
EndTab: the tab goes; Why says why when its stream broke.
EndHeld: the program finished, and the tab stays with its last screen to be read until it is dismissed; Status is what it says over it.

Draft.description: Draft is the prompt in the composer as it stands. The last window to say one is the one whose prompt the next window opens holding; an empty one clears it.

Follow.description: Follow is a link pressed in a pane: a program's (OSC 8) or text the app found on the screen. The core says where it goes, in a Result of the same ID: StatusDone with the URL to open — a URL printed in a box pointed at the port forwarded here for the box's header (the header topic), anything else as written — StatusEnter with the box a discobox link names, or StatusFailed with why it goes nowhere.

box.description: Box is the key of the box the pane is one of, whose server a discobox link that names none is on; empty for a pane that is no box's.
